title: छन्दस् — The Sanskrit Prosody (Meter) Rule Book
subtitle: Compiled from classroom source material on छन्दःशास्त्र (Sanskrit metrics): guru/laghu determination, the गण (triplet) system, and the defining patterns of the major classical metres
source_note: Compiled from a single classroom source PDF ('09_छन्दस्.pdf'), which presents both the general mechanics of Sanskrit prosody (varna, matra, guru/laghu rules, the gana system) and the specific defining patterns (lakshana) of ten named classical metres, each illustrated with real verses (several from well-known devotional/classical sources -- e.g. the Durga/Sarasvati stotra verses, the Vasantatilaka verses on perseverance, the Bhagavad Gita-adjacent Śaṅkara verses). IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL NOTE: छन्दःशास्त्र (prosody), like अलङ्कारशास्त्र, is NOT a Pāṇinian/Aṣṭādhyāyī topic -- its classical authority is Piṅgala's Chandaḥśāstra (Chandas-sūtra), a separate, older treatise with its own sūtra-numbering tradition that this source material does not cite by number. Accordingly ashtadhyayi_ref is null throughout; 'sutra_devanagari' holds the PDF's own memorable verse-rules (which are genuine, widely-used mnemonic verses in the prosody tradition, e.g. यमाताराजभानसलगम्), and book_ref points to Piṅgala's treatise and standard secondary sources for context.

how_to_read.varna: वर्णः / अक्षरम् -- a single syllable: a vowel, or a vowel with its preceding consonant(s)
how_to_read.matra: मात्रा -- the metrical duration/weight of a syllable (1 for लघु, 2 for गुरु)
how_to_read.gana: गणः -- a group of three consecutive syllables, classified into one of 8 named patterns
how_to_read.yati: यतिः -- a caesura/pause point required at a specific syllable-count within a pāda

general_rules.english_name: Definition: chandas as one of the six vedāṅgas; verse (पद्य) vs prose (गद्य)
general_rules.rule: छन्दयति/आह्लादयति इत्यनेन छन्दः -- chandas is so called because it delights/pleases (the reader/listener). It is one of the six वेदाङ्ग (auxiliary Vedic disciplines: शिक्षा, कल्प, व्याकरण, निरुक्त, छन्द, ज्योतिष), and one of the fourteen traditional विद्याs. Literature (साहित्यम्/काव्यम्) divides into पद्यम् (verse) and गद्यम् (prose): पद्यम् is defined as पादचतुष्टययुक्तम् -- text organized into four पादs (metrical quarters/lines), each governed by a fixed count and pattern of syllables; anything not meeting this is गद्यम्.
general_rules.sutra_devanagari: यत् गद्यम् नास्ति तत् पद्यम्, यत् पद्यम् नास्ति तद् गद्यम्। पादचतुष्टययुक्तं पद्यम् (पद्यं चतुष्पात्)।

general_rules.english_name: Syllable (वर्ण) and mora (मात्रा): the basic units of measurement
general_rules.rule: A वर्णः (syllable, for metrical purposes) is a vowel, either alone or preceded by consonant(s) -- a bare consonant alone does NOT count as a syllable. मात्रा is the fixed pronunciation-duration assigned to a syllable's vowel: short vowels (अ इ उ ऋ ऌ) are हृस्व/लघुवर्ण, worth 1 मात्रा (एकमात्रात्मक); long vowels (आ ई ऊ ॠ ए ऐ ओ औ) are दीर्घ/गुरुवर्ण, worth 2 मात्रा (द्विमात्रात्मक).
general_rules.sutra_devanagari: वर्णः (अक्षरम्) — स्वरः अथवा स्वरसहितव्यञ्जनम्। मात्रा — अक्षरगत-स्वरस्य निर्धारितः उच्चारणकालः।
general_rules.process: definitional; foundation for the guru/laghu rule (chandas-3)

examples.gloss: contains exactly two syllables: अ, and वाक् -- a bare consonant is never its own syllable

general_rules.english_name: The five-fold rule for determining whether a syllable is गुरु (heavy) or लघु (light)
general_rules.rule: A syllable is गुरु (heavy) if ANY of the following apply: (1) it carries an अनुस्वार (nasal mark), (2) its vowel is दीर्घ (long), (3) it carries a विसर्ग, (4) it is immediately followed by a consonant-cluster (संयोग) -- i.e. the vowel is followed by two or more consonants before the next vowel, (5) it stands at the very end of a पाद (पादान्त) and metrical necessity calls for it to be treated as heavy even if otherwise short. Any syllable meeting none of these conditions is लघु (light).
general_rules.sutra_devanagari: सानुस्वारश्च दीर्घश्च विसर्गी च गुरूर्भवेत् वर्णः संयोगपूर्वश्च तथा पादान्तगोऽपि वा॥
general_rules.process: पञ्चविधं गुरुत्वनिमित्तम् — अनुस्वार, दीर्घत्व, विसर्ग, संयोगपूर्वत्व, पादान्तत्व

examples.sandhi: सत्य -- स इत्यत्र त्-संयुक्तवर्णस्य पूर्वस्य स गुरुः
examples.gloss: संयोगपूर्व — the स् before the त्य-cluster is गुरु even though स is short

general_rules.english_name: The गण system: syllables are grouped into triplets, classified by a mnemonic sūtra
general_rules.rule: A group of three consecutive syllables is called a गणः. There are exactly eight possible गुरु-लघु patterns for a triplet, and Sanskrit prosody names each with a traditional mnemonic device: the single ten-syllable phrase यमाताराजभानसलगम् encodes all eight गणs as overlapping three-syllable windows (positions 1-2-3 → यगण, 2-3-4 → मगण, 3-4-5 → तगण, 4-5-6 → रगण, 5-6-7 → जगण, 6-7-8 → भगण, 7-8-9 → नगण, 8-9-10 → सगण), where the fixed guru/laghu pattern of the mnemonic word ('य-मा-ता-रा-ज-भा-न-स-ल-गम्', itself alternating heavy/light in a specific way) automatically yields each गण's own pattern by reading three consecutive syllables starting at that position.
general_rules.process: त्रयाणाम् अक्षराणां समूहः एकः गणः; गुरु-लघु-क्रमेण अष्टविधाः गणाः

general_rules.english_name: Mnemonic verse for remembering which gaṇas are 'heavy-biased' vs 'light-biased'
general_rules.rule: A traditional verse summarizes the eight गणs' character: भ-ज-स-गणाः आदि-मध्य-अन्तेषु गौरवं यान्ति (भगण, जगण, सगण are heavy at the start/middle/end respectively of their own guru-laghu positions), while य-र-त-गणाः तत्रैव लाघवं यान्ति (यगण, रगण, तगण are correspondingly light at those same positions) — this is used as a quick check when scanning verse, alongside the direct fact that मगण's all three syllables are गुरु and नगण's all three are लघु.
general_rules.sutra_devanagari: आदिमध्यावसानेषु भजसा यान्ति गौरवम्। यरता लाघवं यान्ति मनौ तु गुरुलाघवम्॥
general_rules.process: स्मरणसाधनम् (mnemonic), not itself an independent rule -- restates chandas-4's 8-gaṇa table in a different form

named_metres.english_name: Anuṣṭubh: the most common classical śloka metre (8 syllables per pāda)
named_metres.rule: अनुष्टुप् has four पादs of 8 syllables each (32 total). Its defining constraint is comparatively loose (most positions are free), except: the 6th syllable of every pāda is always गुरु; the 5th syllable of every pāda is always लघु; in the 2nd and 4th pādas, the 7th syllable is always लघु; in the 1st and 3rd pādas, the 7th syllable is always गुरु.
named_metres.sutra_devanagari: श्लोके षष्ठं गुरु ज्ञेयम् सर्वत्र लघु पञ्चमम्। द्विश्चतुष्पादयोर्ह्रस्वम् सप्तमं दीर्घमन्ययोः॥
named_metres.process: ८ अक्षराणि प्रतिपादम्, ६ष्ठं सर्वत्र गुरु, ५मं सर्वत्र लघु, ७मं पादभेदेन गुरु/लघु

examples.sandhi: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु मातृरूपेण संस्थिता। नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः॥
examples.gloss: the well-known Devī-māhātmya invocation, in anuṣṭubh

examples.sandhi: सरस्वति नमस्तुभ्यं वरदे कामरूपिणि। विद्यारम्भं करिष्यामि सिद्धिर्भवतु मे सदा॥
examples.gloss: the common Sarasvatī invocation before study

named_metres.rule: Each pāda has 14 syllables, following the gaṇa-sequence त-भ-ज-ज-ग-ग (i.e. तगण, भगण, जगण, जगण, then two additional गुरु syllables).

examples.sandhi: प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः। प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः। विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः। प्रारब्धमुत्तमगुणा न परित्यजन्ति॥
examples.gloss: a famous verse on perseverance, in vasantatilakā

named_metres.english_name: Indravajrā, Upendravajrā, and their mixture Upajāti (11-syllable metres)
named_metres.rule: इन्द्रवज्रा: 11 syllables per pāda, gaṇa-pattern त-त-ज-ग-ग. उपेन्द्रवज्रा: 11 syllables, gaṇa-pattern ज-त-ज-ग-ग (differs from इन्द्रवज्रा only in whether the very first syllable is गुरु [इन्द्रवज्रा] or लघु [उपेन्द्रवज्रा]). जब any poem mixes pādas of both types within the same verse, the whole is called उपजाति.
named_metres.sutra_devanagari: स्यादिन्द्रवज्रा यदि तौ जगौ गः — उपेन्द्रवज्रा जतजास्ततो गौ
named_metres.process: ११ अक्षराणि प्रतिपादम्; इन्द्रवज्रा त-त-ज-ग-ग, उपेन्द्रवज्रा ज-त-ज-ग-ग, मिश्रणे उपजातिः

examples.sandhi: त्वमेव माता च पिता त्वमेव त्वमेव बन्धुश्च सखा त्वमेव। त्वमेव विद्या द्रविणं त्वमेव त्वमेव सर्वं मम देव देव॥
हरे मुरारे मधुकैटभारे गोविन्द गोपाल मुकुन्द शौरे। यज्ञेश नारायण कृष्ण विष्णो निराश्रयं मां जगदीश रक्ष॥
examples.gloss: उपजाति verse, mixing both pāda-types (marked उ/इ per pāda in the source)

named_metres.english_name: Śārdūlavikrīḍita: a 19-syllable metre with a mid-line caesura (म-स-ज-स-त-त-ग)
named_metres.rule: 19 syllables per pāda, gaṇa-pattern म-स-ज-स-त-त-ग, with a mandatory यति (caesura/pause) after the 12th syllable (i.e. a 12+7 split).
named_metres.sutra_devanagari: सूर्याश्वैः यदि मः सजौ सततगाः शार्दूलविक्रीडितम्
named_metres.process: १९ अक्षराणि प्रतिपादम्; म-स-ज-स-त-त-ग गणक्रमः; यतिः द्वादशाक्षरे

examples.sandhi: या कुन्देन्दुतुषारहारधवला या शुभ्रवस्त्रावृता। या वीणावरदण्डमण्डितकरा या श्वेतपद्मासना॥ या ब्रह्माच्युतशंकरप्रभृतिभिर्देवैः सदा वन्दिता। सा मां पातु सरस्वती भगवती निःशेषजाड्यापहा॥

named_metres.english_name: Mandākrāntā: a 17-syllable metre with two caesuras (म-भ-न-त-त-ग-ग)
named_metres.rule: 17 syllables per pāda, gaṇa-pattern म-भ-न-त-त-ग-ग, with यति after both the 4th and 10th (equivalently, given as 4-6-7 split points in the source) syllables.

examples.sandhi: कश्चित् कान्ताविरहगुरुणा स्वाधिकारात् प्रमत्तः शापेनास्तंगमितमहिमा वर्षभोग्येण भर्तुः।
examples.gloss: opening verses of Kālidāsa's Meghadūta, the metre's most famous exemplar

named_metres.rule: 17 syllables per pāda, gaṇa-pattern य-म-न-स-भ-ल-ग, with यति after the 6th syllable.
named_metres.process: १७ अक्षराणि प्रतिपादम्; य-म-न-स-भ-ल-ग गणक्रमः; यतिः षष्ठाक्षरे

examples.sandhi: यदा किञ्चिज्ज्ञोऽहं द्विप इव मदान्धः समभवं तदा सर्वज्ञोऽस्मीत्यभवदवलिप्तं मम मनः।
examples.gloss: a well-known verse on the arc of learning and humility

named_metres.english_name: Toṭaka: a 12-syllable metre of four सगणs
named_metres.rule: 12 syllables per pāda, made of exactly four consecutive सगण (।।ऽ, ।।ऽ, ।।ऽ, ।।ऽ).

examples.sandhi: विदिताखिलशास्त्रसुधाजलधे महितोपनिषत्कथितार्थनिधे। हृदये कलये विमलं चरणं भव शङ्कर देशिक मे शरणम्॥
examples.gloss: the famous Toṭakāṣṭakam, traditionally in praise of Śaṅkara's disciple Toṭakācārya

named_metres.english_name: Mālinī: a 15-syllable metre with a mid-line caesura (न-न-म-य-य)
named_metres.rule: 15 syllables per pāda, gaṇa-pattern न-न-म-य-य, with यति after the 8th syllable.
named_metres.process: १५ अक्षराणि प्रतिपादम्; न-न-म-य-य गणक्रमः; यतिः अष्टमाक्षरे

examples.sandhi: प्रथमवयसि पीतं तोयमल्पं भवत्ति शिरसि निहितभाराः नारिकेला नराणाम्। ददति जलमनल्पास्वादमाजीवितान्तं न हि कृतमुपकारं साधवो विस्मरन्ति॥
examples.gloss: a verse comparing coconut palms and gracious people

named_metres.english_name: Āryā: a mora-counted (mātrā-chandas) metre, not a fixed syllable-count metre
named_metres.rule: Unlike all the preceding metres (which are वृत्त-छन्दस्, defined by a fixed COUNT of syllables per pāda), आर्या belongs to the जाति class, defined instead by a fixed count of मात्रा (metrical morae) per pāda -- 12 मात्रा in the 1st pāda, 18 in the 2nd, 12 in the 3rd, and 15 in the 4th, regardless of how many actual syllables are used to reach that count.
named_metres.sutra_devanagari: यस्याः पादे प्रथमे द्वादश मात्रास्तथा तृतीयेऽपि। अष्टादश द्वितीये चतुर्थके पञ्चदश साssर्या॥

summary_counts.status: Covers all metres explicitly named and given a defining lakṣaṇa-verse in the source PDF: anuṣṭubh, vasantatilakā, indravajrā/upendravajrā/upajāti, śārdūlavikrīḍita, mandākrāntā, śikhariṇī, toṭaka, mālinī, āryā -- plus the general vṛtta/jāti, varna/mātrā, guru/laghu, and gaṇa mechanics that underlie all of them.

bibliography: Source PDF: '09_छन्दस्.pdf' -- classroom material on Sanskrit prosody, illustrated with real classical verses (Devī-māhātmya, Meghadūta, Toṭakāṣṭakam, Sarasvatī-vandanā, and others).

Piṅgala. Chandaḥśāstra (Chandas-sūtra) -- the foundational classical treatise on Sanskrit metrics; cited for context, not independently checked against a critical edition for the exact lakṣaṇa-verse readings given in the source PDF.
